---
title: "How stable is the glider to perturbations?"
---

{{< include _model.qmd >}}

```{python}
ENTRY_CEILING = 20.0
SOLVE_BUDGET = 15.0
PROBE_POOL = 120.0
PROBE_SPENT = 55.1

import scipy.optimize as opt_sci
import aerosandbox as asb

opt = optimize_glider_3mm(verbose=False)
c_root, taper, cg_x = get_base_3mm_params(opt)
alpha = float(opt["alpha"])
mass = float(opt["mass"])
weight = mass * 9.81

airplane = make_glider_3mm(c_root, taper, cg_x)

def get_err(V_test):
    op = asb.OperatingPoint(velocity=float(V_test), alpha=alpha)
    aero = asb.AeroBuildup(airplane, op).run()
    return float(aero["L"][0]) - weight

res = opt_sci.root_scalar(get_err, bracket=[0.5, 20.0])
trim_v = res.root

op = asb.OperatingPoint(velocity=trim_v, alpha=alpha)
derivs = asb.AeroBuildup(airplane, op).run_with_stability_derivatives()

cma = float(derivs['Cma'][0])
cnb = float(derivs['Cnb'][0])
clb = float(derivs['Clb'][0])
```

**Answer.** The optimized glider is statically unstable in pitch ($C_{m_{\alpha}}$ = `{python} f"{cma:+.2f}"`) and slightly unstable in roll ($C_{l_{\beta}}$ = `{python} f"{clb:+.3f}"`), but remains stable in yaw ($C_{n_{\beta}}$ = `{python} f"{cnb:+.3f}"`). The optimizer placed the center of gravity behind the neutral point because static stability was never constrained during the trimmed glide optimization.
